packageRules.description: Infrastructure dependencies are NEVER automerged and never merged without reading the plan. On 2026-10-09 a lock-file-only bump of the cloudflare provider (v4.52.9) was merged with a green check; the plan, printed in the PR, said '9 to destroy' and the merge applied it (docs/incidents/2026-10-09-edge-dns.md). An OpenTofu provider or module bump can change what a plan DOES with no line of this repository's own code changing, so the PR is a prompt to run and read the plan, not a change that can be judged by its diff.
prBodyNotes: **Do not merge until you have read the Plan comment(s) on this PR.** Merging applies the stack(s) it touches (push to main). Any `must be replaced` / `destroyed` on a DNS or identity resource turns the check red (see `allow-dns-destroy`); treat that as a signal to stop, not to add the label.

packageRules.description: Providers: let a release age a few days before it is proposed (the 4.52.9 and 5.27.0 releases were merged within hours of the lock bump).

MAJORS are their own PR, opened only when someone asks for it from the dependency dashboard, so that a major bump comes with a deliberate plan. The org preset groups every tf-modules update under one groupName; groupName null takes majors out of that group (a major of one module must never ride in with the minor bumps of another).
Lock-file maintenance is an update like any other: no automerge.
